questions.question: Why does a language model consume token IDs instead of token spellings?
options: Each ID selects a learned row from the model's embedding table
Integer IDs automatically verify the text
IDs remove the need for positional information
Every ID has the same meaning across tokenizers
questions.explanation: The tokenizer-model contract maps each ID to one learned embedding row. The same integer can mean something entirely different in another vocabulary.

questions.question: What can NFC normalization change for a decomposed sequence such as e plus a combining acute accent?
options: It can compose the sequence, changing bytes and later offsets
It always translates the text into English
It adds a beginning-of-sequence token
It guarantees fewer tokens for every tokenizer
questions.explanation: NFC can replace canonically equivalent decomposed sequences with precomposed code points. Segmentation may then change, but a lower token count is not guaranteed.

questions.question: What is the key runtime difference between BPE-style and unigram segmentation?
options: BPE applies saved merge priorities, while unigram scoring selects a high-probability complete piece path
BPE uses IDs, while unigram uses only strings
Unigram tokenizers cannot represent multilingual text
BPE always creates one token per word
questions.explanation: BPE-style tokenizers combine adjacent symbols under learned merge rules. Unigram tokenizers score candidate pieces and choose a complete segmentation path.

questions.question: How should an application handle user text that literally contains a string resembling a system control token?
options: Give it system authority because the spelling matches
Encode it as ordinary untrusted content and insert real control IDs only from trusted application state
Remove all punctuation from every user message
Allow it only when the context window is large
questions.explanation: Control authority comes from trusted structure, not user-selected spelling. Tool authorization and instruction hierarchy still need enforcement outside tokenization.

questions.question: A 4,096-token window reserves 420 fixed input tokens and 512 output tokens. How many tokens remain for document content?
Why can chunk overlap increase production cost?
options: Overlapped tokens are sent in more than one request and are billed or processed repeatedly
Overlap permanently enlarges the model vocabulary
Overlap changes every token ID
Overlap disables output generation
questions.explanation: Overlap preserves some cross-boundary context by duplicating input across adjacent chunks. That duplication consumes additional tokens, latency, and capacity.

questions.question: Which release practice best protects tokenizer-model compatibility?
options: Pin only the vocabulary size
Ship and hash the checkpoint, tokenizer artifacts, special-token map, template, settings, and library versions as one tested bundle
Accept any tokenizer that decodes to readable text
Compare average English token count and skip downstream tests
questions.explanation: Compatibility depends on exact IDs, normalization, segmentation data, special tokens, templates, and runtime behavior. A complete versioned bundle supports reproducible evaluation and rollback.
